nodes.title: Directed modularity transfer between families linked by one residual congruence
nodes.statement: For i=A,B let E_i be a number field and (ρ_i,λ) a family of continuous semisimple two-dimensional representations of G_Q, each defined over a finite extension of (E_i)_λ. Give a finite set S_i and polynomials P_i,q in E_i[X] whose images are the characteristic polynomials of arithmetic Frobenius on ρ_i,λ whenever q is outside S_i and q differs from the residue characteristic of λ; every such member is unramified there. Choose λ_A and λ_B above the same rational prime p, coefficient embeddings into Q̄_p, and stable lattices with isomorphic residual semisimplifications over F̄_p. Both selected characteristic-zero representations are irreducible, odd, finitely ramified and de Rham, of weights {0,k_A−1} and {0,k_B−1}, with k_A,k_B≥2. If one A-member is attached to a normalized cuspidal newform of weight at least two, and the relevant branch hypothesis below holds, then every B-member is attached, after common coefficient extension with compatible algebraic embeddings, to one normalized cuspidal newform g of weight k_B. Under the reducible Pan or ordinary-three branch, the same conclusion follows from the B-family data alone, without a modular A-family or a residual congruence.
hypotheses: Odd irreducible branch: p is odd and the common residual representation restricted to G_Q(ζ_p) is absolutely irreducible. A known modular A-member is the modularity seed; congruence supplies residual modularity for B.
Dyadic branch: p=2 and the common residual image is nonsolvable. Oddness is imposed on the characteristic-zero representations; reduction modulo two cannot detect its determinant sign.

Reducible Pan branch: p≥5 and the selected B-residual semisimplification is χ̄_1⊕χ̄_2; also allow p=3 if (χ̄_1χ̄_2^−1)|G_Q3 differs from ω_3. Characteristic-zero irreducibility remains required. No ordinarity, residual modularity or coefficient-prime Weil–Deligne comparison is assumed.

Exceptional ordinary-three branch: p=3; a specified finite-order character η gives τ=ρ_B,λB⊗η^−1 with residual semisimplification 1⊕ω_3 globally, τ|I_3 upper triangular with quotient 1, and det τ=ψ ε_3^(k_B−1) for ψ of finite order. The normalization is justified by the actual ordinary quotient. Congruence does not establish these hypotheses.

For all good-prime identities, enlarge coefficient number fields and local fields before comparing. No isomorphism between different-characteristic coefficient fields is asserted. Frobenius recognition is applied separately in each fixed residue characteristic.

The family hypotheses are ordinary indexed representation and polynomial data, not an invocation of a compatible-system carrier, existence theorem, strict compatibility or all-member de Rham predicate. Only the selected members need the stated de Rham condition.
proofSteps: If a modular A-member is supplied, identify its good Frobenius polynomials with those of its newform. In the algebraic compositum of coefficient fields the equality is an equality of algebraic numbers, since the chosen local embedding is injective. Embed that identity at λ_A and apply the R01.5 characteristic-polynomial recognition theorem. Thus the selected A-member is modular; no lifting theorem or bad-prime compatibility is used for this propagation.

In the odd irreducible and dyadic cases apply the existing R32.6 transfer-residually-irreducible-odd or transfer-dyadic theorem to the selected congruent pair. In the Pan case apply transfer-residually-reducible to the B-member without a modularity seed. In the exceptional ordinary-three case apply R32.5/p-three-residually-reducible-branch to τ and untwist by η.

The R32.1 weight-of-modular-twist convention identifies the modular witness with a weight-k_B newform g, absorbing the finite-order twist. The selected B-member therefore has g’s good Frobenius polynomials after common algebraic coefficient extension.

Repeat the algebraic-number comparison with P_B,q and use the all-λ newform realizations and R01.5 recognition separately for each B-member. Intersect the two cofinite good-prime sets, also removing its own residue characteristic. Semisimplicity upgrades the resulting semisimplification isomorphism to an isomorphism of the given member. No equality of Weil–Deligne parameters at p is used.

acceptance: A bridge at p=5 may have p in S_B and reducible residual B-member. Given characteristic-zero irreducibility, oddness and de Rham weights {0,3}, Pan produces a weight-four witness without coefficient-prime WD data or a modular A-family.

At p=3 a normalized residual sum 1⊕ω_3 has excluded Pan ratio ω_3 in either ordering. The ordinary-three branch works only after the inertia-quotient and finite-order determinant hypotheses have been checked on B.
At p=2 an isomorphism of residual representations with solvable image does not enter the dyadic branch; nor does residual determinant 1 establish characteristic-zero oddness.
A modular A-family and a residual congruence alone do not enter any branch when B is missing the required local or residual-image conditions.

Within one family, modularity of a member propagates using only good polynomials and semisimplicity, without de Rham conditions at the other coefficient primes. A claimed equality of good polynomials must be checked after specified coefficient embeddings.

A finite chain is handled edge by edge, recording the prime, embeddings, lattices, selected weights and the applicable branch for each directed edge. Reverse traversal requires hypotheses for its new target; a reducible branch can instead start modularity without a seed.
